claims.text: Post-deposition annealing relieves residual stress and reduces defects in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type ribbons.
Post-deposition annealing produces controlled reordering or homogenization of magnetic domains.
Microstructural relaxation directly moderates the first-order magnetostructural transition in FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Annealing-induced relaxation reduces magnetic hysteresis during low-field cycles.
Annealing-induced relaxation broadens the magnetocaloric entropy-change response during low-field cycles.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type ribbons have a single-phase hexagonal structure.
Rapid deposition leaves the target ribbons with high residual stress, substantial defect concentrations, and limited grain size.
Annealing significantly narrows X-ray diffraction peak widths.
Annealing decreases the distribution of exchange interactions and increases magnetic homogeneity.
A more uniform microstructure distributes the magnetostructural transformation over a broader temperature range.
Broadening the transformation reduces its abruptness and hysteresis.
The proposed microstructural homogenization improves refrigerant capacity.
The proposed microstructural homogenization improves heat-exchange rates.
Annealed samples will exhibit a less sharp and more gradual magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit reduced hysteresis in M(H) loops relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing may increase refrigerant capacity through enhanced near-transition magnetic susceptibility.
The as-deposited films have a sharp, hysteretic magnetocaloric entropy change.
High residual stress and defect-induced inhomogeneity limit the heat-exchange efficiency of the as-deposited films.
The predicted benefits apply only within an annealing window that avoids phase transformation and excessive grain growth.

contradictions.description: The mediator asserts that annealing narrows the distribution of exchange interactions and increases magnetic homogeneity, whereas the mechanism invokes a more broadly distributed transformation to explain entropy broadening. No additional source of transition-temperature dispersion is given to reconcile greater homogeneity with a broader transition.
